title: I'm a night security guard at a furniture showroom. Every morning, the same display bed has been slept in.
transcript:
I'm a night security guard at a furniture showroom. Every morning, the same display bed has been slept in. The showroom closes at nine. I lock up, walk the floor once an hour, and sit at the desk by the loading dock watching twelve camera feeds. Nobody else has keys except the manager, and she lives two towns over.

The first morning, the sales staff found the blue bed in the back corner unmade. Pillows dented, blanket pulled back. They blamed me. I hadn't touched it.

The next night I watched that corner on camera nine all shift. Nothing. At six I walked over, and the blanket was turned down, and the pillow was warm.

So I sat on a recliner across the aisle and stayed there. Just after three in the morning, the lights in that section flickered. When they came back, the mattress had sunk in the middle, slowly, like someone heavy was lying down. The blanket rose and fell. I could hear breathing.

I didn't move until the sun came up.

That afternoon the manager called me. She said the blue bed finally sold, and the buyer had asked for the security guard by name to help with delivery.

I asked her what the address was.

She read me mine.

It's being delivered tomorrow.
